question.text: For income tax purposes, a commodity derivative transaction is considered speculative if:

answer.text: It is settled without delivery and is not part of a documented hedging strategy
All commodity derivative transactions are speculative
It involves physical delivery of the commodity
It is traded on a recognized exchange

explanation.text: The Logic: Under general Indian income-tax practice, a commodity derivative transaction that is cash-settled (no physical delivery) and not supported by a documented hedge of an underlying physical exposure is typically treated as a speculative transaction for tax purposes. Delivery-settled transactions, and transactions linked to a bona fide hedge, generally avoid speculative classification. The Trap: Not all commodity derivative transactions are automatically speculative — physical delivery or proper hedge documentation changes the result. Merely trading on a recognized exchange does not by itself determine speculative status. Note: The Series XVI Commodity Derivatives workbook pages reviewed define hedgers and speculators and discuss long/short speculative positions, but do not articulate this income-tax rule with the documented-hedge condition. The framing above reflects general industry/tax practice rather than a workbook citation.
